verdict.rationale: Bun documents built-in conversion: running `bun install` in a project without `bun.lock` automatically migrates `yarn.lock` (v1), `package-lock.json` (lockfileVersion 2–4) and `pnpm-lock.yaml`. It also honors npm `overrides` and Yarn `resolutions`, and can write a Yarn lockfile alongside `bun.lock`. A community comment calls switching cost zero; one Windows crash report only speculates about a link to old package-locks, which is not a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: migration support for Yarn Berry (v2+) lockfiles, independent hands-on confirmation of lockfile conversion fidelity, documented conversion of pnpm-specific workspace config.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can migrate an existing project from the incumbent tool with documented import or conversion tooling

citations.quote: When you run `bun install` in a project without a `bun.lock`, Bun automatically migrates existing lockfiles:
It's a standalone tool that works in existing Node.js projects; if your project has a `package.json`, you can use `bun install`.
Bun supports npm's `"overrides"` and Yarn's `"resolutions"` in `package.json`.
Didn't prevent me from switching to Bun as the cost is 0.
